title: Steelyard Haul-Off brand rollout: rebuild the raster logo as clean production vector artwork, derive the mask-polarity mark family, neutralize six mixed-light fleet shots to one house white point, and data-merge a per-placement brand spec book
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork logo-vectorization + brand-identity-kit brief for a junk-removal / cleanout / hauling company that had its logo only as a low-res raster and needed print-ready vector artwork plus wrap/shirt/print variations and a color + type reference. The real client and city are laundered to the fictional 'Steelyard Haul-Off' (Central Florida hauler); no real company, person, competition, product, or trademark is named or depicted, and no proprietary craft-software brand names appear in any task-facing field (the mark is rebuilt as original vector geometry traced from the client's own supplied artwork, never extracted from a font or a real logo). REASONABLY ENRICHED and REPAIRED against the audit that flagged this task (G4: the 'brand kit' was punted to a font-recommend JSON instead of a real designed artifact; G5: color_overlay/fill_area were mis-used to fake knockouts; plus a monogram/wordmark naming mismatch). This rebuild fixes all three and raises the bar: (1) the client hands TWO look-alike references of the same mark - a flat digital export AND a phone photo of the same mark vinyl-applied to a truck panel - and only the flat export can be traced; the curved-metal photo, if traced, returns garbage paths and must instead become a cut-out application packshot (a trippable trace-triage). (2) The monogram is a deliberately OPEN-COUNTER stencil-block 'SY' (the letters S and Y carry no fully-enclosed counters) precisely so the reversed/knockout treatments are honestly producible with the connector - a dark-ground knockout of an enclosed-counter mark is NOT connector-doable and is avoided by design. (3) The 'brand photography' the kit needs is restored as SIX real fleet/crew/yard shots taken on different days under different light, each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card, that must be neutralized to ONE house white point. (4) The color sheet and the type are actually SET, as real copy bound into a hand-authored single-record .indd page-layout template and data-merged one page per placement - the designed artifact the agent owns, not a hand-off. Every step is a real Adobe connector action; nothing on the CANNOT list is used.
one_line_ask: Rebuild Steelyard Haul-Off's mark as clean production vector artwork from the client's supplied logo, derive the full mark family (scalable color master, two-tone monogram icon, one-color cut path, a reversed knockout, and a lime-on-black hero) using the right mechanic for each, deliver a real-world application packshot proof of the mark, neutralize six mixed-lighting fleet photos to one house white point by eye against their in-frame grey cards, and merge a hand-authored page-layout template against the placement roster into one press-ready brand spec sheet per placement.
full_brief:
Steelyard Haul-Off is a junk-removal, cleanout and light-demolition company rolling out new fleet and crew branding across box trucks, roll-off containers, crew tees, car magnets, yard signs and a storefront window. Their palette is black, safety lime-green and steel grey, and the mark is a bold stencil-block 'SY' monogram sitting above the 'STEELYARD' wordmark and a thin tagline. They need a professional, print-and-wrap-ready brand rollout package.

What you are given: TWO reference images of the mark (they only ever had it as raster, no vector source on file), six recent photographs of their fleet, crew and yard taken for the brand book, a placement roster listing every surface the brand will land on with its substrate, size, minimum clear space and required colorway, and a hand-built page-layout template for the spec sheets.

The job:
1) Produce the clean, scalable vector MASTER of the full lockup, print-ready with crisp edges and the black / lime / steel-grey palette intact - work from whichever of the two supplied references actually rebuilds into clean vector geometry, and get the other one delivered in the form it is actually good for.
2) From the master, build the rest of the mark FAMILY: a two-tone monogram-only icon for app tiles and embroidery; a single-color version for one-color screen-print, vinyl cutting and stamps; a reversed treatment that reads correctly on dark substrates; and a high-impact lime-on-black hero to splash large across a trailer side. Each of these is a different production need - use the treatment that genuinely produces each one, not one blanket effect relabelled five times.
3) Make the six brand photographs read as ONE set. They were shot on different days under different light, so out of the folder they do not match. Each frame carries an 18% grey card in shot as a reference; neutralize every frame to it so the whole set lands on one common, true house white point with a subtle honest daylight warmth - deep shadows that stay open, highlights on chrome and hi-vis that do not blow. Because each frame started under different light, matching the OUTPUT means each frame needs its OWN correction reasoned from its OWN card - a single blanket setting across the batch will not match, and one of the shots is of a genuinely lime-green subject under clean light, so do not chase a cast that is not there. When done, hand back the white-balance and exposure moves you settled on per frame so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed, and crop the grey card out of the finals.
4) Assemble the deliverable: we have hand-built the page-layout template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the placement's logo colorway, one for its brand photo). Merge it against the roster so every placement gets its own single-page spec sheet - the surface name, substrate, size, clear-space rule and palette callouts (hex / CMYK / spot-ink) bound as copy, with the correct colorway artwork and the matching graded photo dropped in - and hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every placement, one page per placement, the flagship placement first.

Hard rules: original vector geometry rebuilt from our supplied artwork, no from-scratch redraw, no generative fill or object removal, no compositing, no upscaling; the color sheet and type are actually set through the merge, not handed off.

inputs.name: steelyard_ref_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat, slightly low-resolution company logo artwork file for a junk-removal / hauling business, rendered as clean flat vector-style art (no photographic texture): a bold geometric STENCIL-BLOCK 'SY' monogram - the S and Y drawn as chunky stencil letterforms with bridge gaps and NO fully-enclosed interior counters - in safety lime-green (#8DC63F) and black, sitting above a heavy condensed sans-serif wordmark reading 'STEELYARD' in black, above a thin steel-grey tagline 'HAUL-OFF · CLEANOUTS · DEMOLITION'. Black, lime-green and steel-grey palette only, crisp readable type, no gradients, no drop shadows, no bevels. The whole lockup is very slightly rotated about 2.5 degrees clockwise as if exported off-axis, set on a near-white #F4F4F2 background with faint JPEG-style compression softness around the edges. Flat logo artwork, roughly 3000 px on the long edge, not glossy 3D.
inputs.realism_notes: TRACEABLE SOURCE. This is the clean flat artwork export the mark can actually be rebuilt from: crisp flat color, legible type, a genuine ~2.5° skew that image_auto_straighten must correct before tracing, and a near-white (not pure-white) ground that warrants a background knock so the trace has no halo. The monogram is deliberately an OPEN-COUNTER stencil 'SY' (S and Y carry no enclosed counters) - this is the load-bearing constraint that makes the reversed / knockout treatments HONEST: a solid one-color silhouette of an open-counter mark still reads correctly, whereas remove_background cannot punch open an enclosed interior counter on a dark ground, so an enclosed-counter mark could not be delivered as a dark-ground knockout. It is handed to the agent as 'our logo' with no marker distinguishing it from the truck-panel photo; the agent must decide which of the two rebuilds into clean vector. Declared at ~3000 px so the master trace and the monogram crop never upscale.
inputs.hardness_role: trace-triage correct source; open-counter design enabling honest knockouts

inputs.name: steelyard_ref_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal phone snapshot of the SAME stencil 'SY' + 'STEELYARD' logo as it is currently vinyl-applied to the door panel of a white box truck, shot outdoors in a parking lot at a slight three-quarter angle. The logo sits on the gently curved, riveted steel door with visible panel seams, a couple of rivets crossing the artwork, road-dust grime along the bottom, and a bright specular glare band from the sky sliding across the lime-green so the color is uneven, plus soft reflections of the surroundings. Real vehicle photography, shallow-ish depth, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, roughly 3500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: TRACE-TRIAGE DECOY. It looks like 'a second copy of the logo' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of the mark on curved, riveted, glare-streaked, dusty metal - the perspective skew, panel curvature, rivets, grime and specular banding would all become garbage paths if fed to image_vectorize. It must NOT go anywhere near the tracer. Its only correct use is as a real-world application packshot: knock the parking-lot background off with image_remove_background to isolate the truck-door subject as a clean cut-out proof for the spec book. A naive agent that traces it (because it, too, 'is the logo') produces an unusable vector; the failure is invisible until the SVG path data is opened. Carries NO grey card - it is a reference/proof image, not one of the six calibrated brand photos, so it is graded/measured on nothing and simply cut out. Declared at ~3500 px so the packshot downscales, never upscales.
inputs.hardness_role: trace-triage decoy; correct route is remove_background packshot, never vectorize

inputs.name: fleet_box_truck.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution DSLR/mirrorless camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of a clean white box truck parked at a hauling company yard, three-quarter front view, shot in warm low late-afternoon sunlight giving a strong amber cast, the frame very slightly tilted about 3 degrees. A photographic 18% neutral grey card is clipped to the wing mirror in the lower-left of frame as a white-balance reference. Real vehicle paint, asphalt, and yard clutter behind; candid documentary feel, no CGI gloss, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #1 of the matched set. Warm amber evening cast + ~3° tilt: the correct move (kept out of the brief and step notes) is to straighten, then cool the white balance until its in-frame grey card reads neutral and it lands on the shared house white point, holding a light honest warmth. Its correction differs from every other frame. Real-camera scale so the placement crop downscales into the merge frame at ~300 DPI, never upscales. Grey card on the mirror is croppable out of the final.

inputs.name: fleet_rolloff_container.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of a large steel roll-off dumpster container at a yard under flat cool overcast light giving a bluish cast, level horizon. A photographic 18% neutral grey card rests on the container lip at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference. Real weathered steel texture, rust streaks, gravel ground; documentary feel, no CGI, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #2. Cool overcast bluish cast, level (no straighten needed): the correct move (undisclosed in task-facing fields) is to WARM the white balance until its grey card reads neutral to the shared house white point - the opposite direction from the warm truck frame, which is why one blanket batch setting cannot match the set. Real-camera scale for downscale-only into the merge.

inputs.name: fleet_crew_tee.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of a folded safety lime-green (hi-vis) crew t-shirt laid on a neutral grey studio bench under clean, near-neutral balanced light, level frame. A photographic 18% neutral grey card lies beside it as a white-balance reference. The shirt's lime-green is vivid and true; real fabric weave and seam texture; documentary feel, no CGI, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #3 - THE TRAP FRAME. It was shot under clean near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral, and the vivid lime-green is the REAL product color, not a cast. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only a small exposure/tone match to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool frames / cool the warm frames' logic, or that 'kills an imagined green cast', will drive this card off-neutral and strip the safety-lime the brand is built on. The decision must be read from THIS card, not the batch. Undisclosed in the brief and step notes - the diagnosis lives only here. Real-camera scale.

inputs.name: fleet_yard_sign.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of a metal yard/road sign post at the hauling yard entrance under harsh direct noon sun, slightly overexposed with a faintly cool sky cast, level frame. A photographic 18% neutral grey card is taped to the post at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference. Real galvanized-metal and painted-sign texture, hard shadows, blown-risk highlights on the bright areas; documentary feel, no CGI, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #4. Overexposed harsh noon with a faint cool cast: the correct move (undisclosed) is to pull exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown areas AND warm slightly to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point - a combined tonal-plus-WB correction different again from the others. Real-camera scale for downscale-only merge placement.

inputs.name: fleet_car_magnet.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of a magnetic vehicle door sign on a sedan parked in open shade, flat and slightly underexposed with a cool shade cast, level frame. A photographic 18% neutral grey card is wedged against the door at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference. Real car paint and magnet-vinyl texture, soft shade light; documentary feel, no CGI, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #5. Cool open-shade cast, flat and underexposed: the correct move (undisclosed) is to LIFT exposure and add contrast, then warm the white balance to neutralize its grey card to the shared house white point - the dominant problem here is tonal, unlike the truck frame's WB-led correction. Real-camera scale.

inputs.name: fleet_storefront.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-resolution camera capture, ~3800 px long edge, of the company's small storefront/dispatch office window from the sidewalk, lit by mixed warm interior light spilling out and cool daylight on the glass, the frame tilted about 4 degrees. A photographic 18% neutral grey card sits on the window ledge at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference. Real glass reflections, brick, and signage; documentary feel, no CGI, grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Brand-photo #6 - the flagship/hero placement photo. Mixed warm-interior + cool-daylight light and a ~4° tilt: the correct move (undisclosed) is to straighten, then settle a balanced white balance that neutralizes its grey card to the shared house white point despite the mixed sources. Real-camera scale so the hero placement crop downscales into the merge frame at ~300 DPI.

inputs.name: steelyard_specbook_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait brand-placement spec sheet - ONE placement per page. It carries live data-merge placeholder fields <<placement>>, <<substrate>>, <<size_in>>, <<min_clearspace>>, <<colorway_note>>, and <<brand_palette>>, PLUS TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a logo-artwork frame bound to @logo (the placement's correct colorway artwork) and a brand-photo frame bound to @photo (that placement's grey-card-neutralized fleet photo). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, both images reach the page ONLY as merge binds through these two frames. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record spec sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. TWO image columns (@logo, @photo) mean the merge resolves two AGENT-PRODUCED assets per row - the colorway artwork the agent traced/derived AND that placement's graded photo - so every agent-produced asset has a real, connector-doable path onto the page with no free-form placement. Mirrors the two-image-column merge pattern proven in the bakery line-sheet task.

inputs.name: steelyard_placement_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns placement,substrate,size_in,min_clearspace,colorway_note,brand_palette,@logo,@photo holding 6 rows, one per brand placement, the flagship placement FIRST. Rows: (1) Storefront window hero graphic - substrate 'Frosted glass, dark vinyl backer', a large size, clear-space rule, colorway_note 'High-impact lime mark on solid black field', @logo naming the lime-on-black hero artwork file, @photo naming the storefront graded photo; (2) Box-truck door graphics - 'Cast wrap vinyl over white panel', colorway_note 'Full-color master lockup on light substrate', @logo naming the color master file, @photo the box-truck graded photo; (3) Roll-off container - 'Painted / decal on dark steel', colorway_note 'Reversed one-color mark for dark substrate', @logo naming the reversed-knockout file, @photo the roll-off graded photo; (4) Crew tee (front) - 'Screen-print on charcoal fabric', colorway_note 'Single-color mark for one-color print', @logo naming the one-color file, @photo the crew-tee graded photo; (5) Car magnet - 'Magnetic vinyl on light door', colorway_note 'Full-color master lockup', @logo naming the color master file, @photo the car-magnet graded photo; (6) Yard sign - 'Painted aluminum panel', colorway_note 'Two-tone monogram icon', @logo naming the icon file, @photo the yard-sign graded photo. brand_palette holds the black / lime / steel-grey hex + CMYK + spot-ink callouts as one text string. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the two @image-path columns @logo and @photo.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's brand-color-sheet and per-surface colorway requirements as bound copy; headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct colorway artwork, AND the matching graded photo per placement. The @logo column references AGENT-PRODUCED variant filenames (the agent must produce each colorway under the referenced name using the correct mechanic) and the @photo column references the agent's graded photo filenames - the answer to the trace-triage sits in NO field here; the roster only encodes the per-surface colorway BRAND RULE, never which raw reference to trace. Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six finished sheets, page 1 the flagship storefront hero.

outputs.name: steelyard_master_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Clean scalable vector MASTER of the full lockup (stencil SY monogram + STEELYARD wordmark + tagline), crisp closed paths, transparent ground, black / lime / steel-grey palette preserved. Produced by a whole-raster color trace (image_vectorize) of the straightened, cast-corrected, background-knocked source artwork - the print-and-wrap-ready master the rest of the family derives from. Original geometry rebuilt from the supplied source artwork, never from a font file.

outputs.name: steelyard_icon_mark.svg
outputs.spec: Two-tone monogram-only icon: the open-counter stencil 'SY' in lime + black as separate closed shapes, transparent ground, for app tiles, embroidery and social avatars. Produced by cropping the cleaned master to the monogram block and running a whole-crop COLOR trace (distinct mechanic from the one-color silhouette below).

outputs.name: steelyard_mark_1color.svg
outputs.spec: Single-color version of the monogram: one solid silhouette (fill collapsed to one color) for one-color screen-print, vinyl cutting, stamps and embroidery weeding. Produced by feeding a glyph SELECTION of the monogram to image_vectorize, which returns a single-color silhouette - the deliberately DIFFERENT vectorize polarity from the two-tone icon. Honest because the mark is open-counter: the silhouette still reads as SY.

outputs.name: steelyard_mark_white_on_black.png
outputs.spec: Reversed colorway swatch: the open-counter monogram as a solid WHITE silhouette on the brand-black field, hi-res PNG, for dark substrates (dark shirts, dark steel, dark wrap panels). Produced by a solid white fill of the isolated monogram (image_fill_area on the monogram selection) then setting the surrounding canvas to brand-black (change_background_color) - not a whole-image overlay and not a select->invert->fill knockout. Honest only because the monogram carries no enclosed counters.

outputs.name: steelyard_hero_lime_on_black.png
outputs.spec: Creative hero: the open-counter monogram as a solid high-impact lime silhouette on solid brand-black, hi-res PNG, to splash large across a trailer/container side. Produced by a solid lime fill of the isolated monogram (image_fill_area) then a brand-black canvas (change_background_color). Lime achieved by masked solid fill, black by the canvas color - no generative fill, no compositing.

outputs.name: steelyard_application_packshot.png
outputs.spec: Real-world application packshot: the mark shown applied in situ, its subject isolated from the surrounding background by image_remove_background to a transparent ground, hi-res raster with NO vector paths. A downscale/reframe of the ~3500 px source, never an upscale.

outputs.name: graded_fleet_photos_x6
outputs.spec: Six grey-card-neutralized brand photos delivered as the placement-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) that the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) - the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared house white point while holding a subtle honest daylight warmth, no product/paint color forced off (the hi-vis crew-tee frame holds its true lime); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered placement crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by the agent's report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied per frame.

outputs.name: Steelyard_Brand_Placement_Specbook.pdf
outputs.spec: The designed deliverable: exactly six press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait brand-placement spec sheets - ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) - exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge; each page binds its placement / substrate / size / clear-space rule / colorway note and the black-lime-steel palette callouts verbatim from the roster, with the placement's correct colorway artwork dropped into the @logo frame and its matching grey-card-neutralized brand photo into the @photo frame (both by merge bind, never free-form placement). ~300 DPI print quality; page 1 is the flagship storefront hero (no per-record named export - the whole merged document is exported in one call, and the hero is simply its first page).

connector_workflow.inputs_from: steelyard_ref_01.png, steelyard_ref_02.png, fleet_box_truck.jpg, fleet_rolloff_container.jpg, fleet_crew_tee.jpg, fleet_yard_sign.jpg, fleet_car_magnet.jpg, fleet_storefront.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Single ingest: bring the two logo references and the six brand photos into Creative Cloud storage. Every later step consumes a named prior output; this is the only image ingest (the authored template and roster are supplied inputs consumed at the merge). Plumbing, not the difficulty.

MASTER branch. Rectify the off-axis tilt on the flat logo artwork so edges are true before any trace - the only tool that rectifies a tilt. Report the correcting angle. Consumes the flat logo reference.

Author a clean-up pass by eye: neutralize any residual cast and push contrast/clarity so the black, lime and steel-grey separate hard-edged for the trace. Primitive-built adjustments (not a preset, not auto-tone). Report the moves applied.
Knock the near-white ground to true transparency so the trace inherits no halo or fringe. remove_background -> transparency, isolating the outer background only. Consumes step 3.

DELIVERABLE (master): whole-raster COLOR trace of the prepared transparent lockup into the scalable vector master - lime, black and steel-grey come through as separate closed shapes. Trace of a prepared raster, no selection. Consumes step 4.

Reframe the cleaned transparent lockup to the SY monogram block, dropping the wordmark and tagline, to make a monogram-only working raster. Prompt-aware crop / downscale-only; never canvas-extend, never upscale. Consumes step 4.
DELIVERABLE (two-tone icon): whole-crop COLOR trace of the monogram block so lime and black stay separate closed shapes. Consumes step 6.

Semantically select 'the SY monogram mark' on the monogram crop to isolate the mark shape from its transparent surround - the shared mask for the single-color and reversed treatments below. A real object selection (not a hue or a coordinate region). Consumes step 6.

DELIVERABLE (one-color): vectorize the monogram SELECTION, which returns a single-color solid silhouette - the one-color screen-print / vinyl-cut path. Deliberately the DIFFERENT vectorize polarity from step 7's whole-crop color trace: swap them and the icon loses its two-tone or the cut path arrives as unweedable color art. Consumes step 8.
Solid-fill the monogram selection pure WHITE (image_fill_area is solid color only) on the monogram crop, leaving a white silhouette on transparent. Consumes the step-6 crop + step-8 mask.

DELIVERABLE (reversed): set the transparent surround to solid brand-black -> white open-counter monogram on black for dark substrates. change_background_color fills the existing transparent canvas; it does not outpaint or enlarge. Consumes step 10.
Solid-fill the same monogram selection with high-impact brand LIME on the monogram crop, leaving a lime silhouette on transparent. Consumes the step-6 crop + step-8 mask.
DELIVERABLE (hero): set the transparent surround to solid brand-black -> the lime-on-black hero. Canvas color only, no compositing. Consumes step 12.

DELIVERABLE (application packshot): isolate the truck-door subject from its parking-lot background to a clean transparent cut-out. Consumes the truck-panel reference photo directly - a photograph routed to background removal, not to the tracer. remove_background -> transparency.
BRAND-PHOTO set. Level the box-truck frame's tilt before grading so the placement crop is measured against a true horizon. Report the angle. Consumes the box-truck photo.

Neutralize this frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame 18% grey card, reasoning THIS frame's own white-balance/exposure correction and holding a subtle honest warmth; deep shadows open, chrome highlights protected. Never read a pixel value - dial until the card looks neutral and REPORT the temperature/tint/exposure applied. Primitive-built (not a preset, not auto-tone). Retain this pre-crop master (card in frame) as the neutrality artifact. Consumes step 15.

Crop the neutralized frame to the placement image frame, framing on the subject with the grey card cropped OUT - this card-removed crop is what binds into the sheet. Downscale-only reframe from the ~3800 px source, never upscale, never canvas-extend. Consumes step 16.

Neutralize the roll-off container frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame grey card, reasoning its own correction (this frame is level, no straighten). Hold the shared warmth; keep steel tones honest. Report the applied moves. Retain this pre-crop master as the neutrality artifact. Consumes the roll-off photo.
Crop to the placement image frame, grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only. Consumes step 18.

Neutralize the crew-tee frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame grey card, reasoning THIS frame's own correction from its OWN card rather than the batch, and keep the subject's true color intact. Report the applied moves. Retain this pre-crop master as the neutrality artifact. Consumes the crew-tee photo.
Crop to the placement image frame, grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only. Consumes step 20.

Neutralize the yard-sign frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame grey card, reasoning its own combined tonal-and-white-balance correction and recovering the bright areas without clipping. Report the applied moves. Retain this pre-crop master as the neutrality artifact. Consumes the yard-sign photo.
Crop to the placement image frame, grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only. Consumes step 22.

Neutralize the car-magnet frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame grey card, reasoning its own correction (lift the flat/underexposed tone, then balance) so it matches the set. Report the applied moves. Retain this pre-crop master as the neutrality artifact. Consumes the car-magnet photo.
Crop to the placement image frame, grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only. Consumes step 24.
Level the storefront frame's tilt before grading. Report the angle. Consumes the storefront photo.

Neutralize the storefront frame to the shared house white point by eye against its in-frame grey card, reasoning a balanced correction despite the mixed light sources so it lands on the set target. Report the applied moves. Retain this pre-crop master as the neutrality artifact. Consumes step 26.
Crop to the flagship placement image frame, grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only. The six graded crops now share one house white point, each neutralized to its own card. Consumes step 27.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: steelyard_master_logo.svg, steelyard_icon_mark.svg, steelyard_mark_1color.svg, steelyard_mark_white_on_black.png, steelyard_hero_lime_on_black.png, truck_graded, rolloff_graded, tee_graded, sign_graded, magnet_graded, storefront_graded
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the five colorway artworks and the six graded placement photos, under the exact filenames the roster's @logo and @photo columns reference, so the merge can resolve each row's two images.
